whatItIs.text: Milled wheat with the bran and germ removed, leaving the starchy endosperm; its moderate protein gives reliable structure to most home baking.

historyNote.text: Wheat was first cultivated in the Fertile Crescent around 9600 BC and now grows on more land than any other food crop — its gluten is so useful that world trade in wheat exceeds that of all other crops combined.

howToChoose.text: Buy the bag size you will finish in a few months; check the protein note only for bread baking (bread flour, higher), and keep bleached vs unbleached in mind for texture-critical bakes.

storage.text: Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dark cupboard; wholemeal flours spoil faster than white. The rulebook has the details.

foodSafetyRef.note: flour storage guidance lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: A cup of flour thickens any soup or stew (bloom it in butter first), and small amounts turn into pancakes, roux, or a crisp coating for anything fried.

substitutions.note: chewier, stronger; fine for most bakes
for structure-baked goods; texture slightly denser
